content.content:
1	# Design document — carwatch
2	
3	> **WEDNESDAY REVIEW — delete this box, and every 🟨 / 📏 note, before submitting.**
4	> 🟨 **TEAM** = decide or review together. 📏 **DRIVE** = replace with a number from the
5	> first Forester drive (`firstcap`, `pidforester`). Checklist:
6	>
7	> - [ ] Sign, change or reject every review-queue entry this doc cites (`DECISIONS.md`).
8	> - [ ] Decide the fault-area rows in §3 and fill the ownership map in §9.
9	> - [ ] Drive numbers into §1, §3 and §5; Lance's power numbers into §6.
10	> - [ ] Three-isolated-workers check: design-only reader, BOM-only buyer, wiring-only
11	>   builder each succeed from their own part.
12	> - [ ] Render to PDF: 5 pages or fewer without this box.
13	
14	**User and problem.** Lance drives a 2015 CR-V daily, and nothing reads his engine's
15	sensors except a check-engine light that speaks only once something has failed. carwatch
16	is a box that boots at every key-on, records every Mode 01 sensor through a Bluetooth
17	OBD2 dongle, learns *this* car's normal, and flags behavior that leaves it before the
18	light would. It is also tested on Camden's 2008 Forester (D-022). **Claim (D-021):** it
19	learns the normal of the car it is installed in, flags behavior outside it and names the
20	likely fault area, with measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.
21	
22	## 1. Architecture
23	
24	```text
25	OBD2 port -- OBDLink LX (Bluetooth SPP, D-019)   DS18B20 cabin probe (D-037)
26	   ~~ RFCOMM ~~> BlueZ -> rfcomm tty -> /dev/obd    1-Wire -> kernel w1-gpio -> sysfs
27	  obdd    Mode 01, one outstanding, ~10-25 req/s   ambientd   one read every 2 s
28	    | ring 1: SPSC, ~10-25 samples/s                  | ring 2: SPSC, 0.5 samples/s
29	    +------------------------+------------------------+  shared memory, refuse when full
30	                             v
31	  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
32	    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
33	    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
34	    v
35	  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
36	    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
37	    v
38	  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,
39	    ^            1-4 Hz pulse = alive; steady, except yellow at boot = not running (D-027)
40	    | UDS, on demand
41	  obdctl (CLI); statusd: page + report --> phone on the box's Wi-Fi (D-013, D-043)
42	power: owner's USB-C charger -> power block + supercapacitor -> Pi 4 (D-024)
43	```
44	
45	Rates are estimates until the first drive (`firstcap`); the logging tool reaches 22
46	requests a second on `obdsim`. One reply or probe reading is one sample, one record and
47	one analysis step. Queries go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the
48	answer (D-043); `analyzed` never reads a ring (D-031).
49	
50	> 📏 **DRIVE:** measured request rate, reply-time p50/p99 and PID count replace the
51	> estimates here and in §5.
52	
53	## 2. Mechanism mapping
54	
55	D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: these rates never stress
56	a ring, and 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to us (D-029, D-037).
57	
58	| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
59	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
60	| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold crank, pulled cable; D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cuts of the Pi's 5 V rail mid-write; records lost per cut |
61	| E | `supervisor`, `src/ipc/` | A recorder that dies silently harms an owner who thinks it is on duty. Analysis, the least trusted code, must not take capture or storage down (B.2), and each sensor source has its own process, so a hung link cannot stop the probe (D-037) | `kill -9` each child 20×: detection, recovery, fd leaks |
62	
63	**Two distinct sensors that cooperate (handout §3.1).** The DS18B20 and the car's
64	coolant and intake-air sensors are different devices on different buses, read by
65	different processes (D-037). After hours off (the clock says how long, D-030) all three
66	should agree at key-on; the one that disagrees is the suspect. The engine's own sensors
67	are distinct transducers the dongle only carries, and every diagnostic fuses at least two
68	(D.4). "Both sensors alive" (M2) is a real Mode 01 capture plus a probe reading; "through
69	the pipeline" (M3) is both as committed records labeled `live`.
70	
71	## 3. Analysis: how normal is learned and a fault area named
72	
73	All our code (handout §3.3; D.1, D.2). Per committed sample, `analyzed` (1) bins by
74	rpm × load × coolant temperature, so a cold idle is never compared with a warm cruise;
75	(2) keeps per-bin running mean and covariance (Welford), in A/B checkpoints; (3) scores the
76	Mahalanobis distance from the bin's baseline, which fires when a *partnership* breaks;
77	(4) fits Theil–Sen slopes of residuals across drives; (5) names the area with our
78	classifier (trained in `tools/train/`, inference in C; without weights, 1–4 still flag);
79	(6) surfaces verdicts through a hysteresis-and-dwell state machine (D.3).
80	
81	| Fault area (D-021) | Cooperating sensors | Signature | Induced by (E.2) |
82	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
83	| Cooling | coolant, intake temp, ambient (PID 0x46, else the probe), load, speed | warm-up slope or warm settling temperature off its bin's normal for the same ambient and load | cardboard over the radiator |
84	| Air/fuel | fuel trims, MAP or MAF, rpm, O2 | long-term trim rising at idle with idle MAP, shrinking with load | a small vacuum line opened |
85	| Sensor/electrical | the failed PID and its usual partners; module voltage; at a cold start, coolant, intake temp and the probe | one PID absent or flat while its partners move; after a long soak, one temperature off the other two | a sensor unplugged |
86	| Unknown | all | residual high, no area matches | — |
87	
88	No row can be called by one threshold on one value: each compares sensors that normally
89	move together, inside one bin (D.4). 📏 **DRIVE:** strike any sensor the survey shows the
90	Forester does not publish.
91	
92	> 🟨 **TEAM DECIDES (Wednesday):** the fault-area rows, signatures and bin axes above are
93	> Claude's draft from D-021 and D.2 (§10). Confirm, change or replace each row, and then
94	> delete this note.
95	
96	## 4. Failure-mode table
97	
98	Log lines are `<process> <level> <event> key=value` with `src`; the table names the event.
99	
100	| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log event |
101	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
102	| adapter | Bluetooth drops | `read` 0/`EIO`, `POLLHUP` | reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff | `link_lost`, `reconnected` |
103	| adapter | garbage or timeouts | parse failure; timeout | 3 in a row: `ATZ`, then reopen | `reply_bad`, `adapter_reset` |
104	| adapter | engine off, key in ACC | `0100` gets `NO DATA` | poll `0100` every few s, record nothing | `ecu_silent` |
105	| ECU | a sensor unplugged or failed | 5 `NO DATA` in a row; or pinned or flat while its partners move, MIL on (PID 0101) | mark absent or suspect, retry each minute. ECUs often substitute a value and light the CEL: not caught before the light | `pid_absent`, `pid_flat`, `mil_on`, `pid_present` |
106	| probe | unplugged, broken wire, bad read | device gone from sysfs; CRC `NO`; the 85.0 °C power-on value | mark absent, retry every 10 s; cold-soak check off, reported | `sensor_absent`, `sensor_present`, `reply_bad` |
107	| any child | crash, `kill -9` | `waitpid` | restart with backoff; others run on | `child_exit`, `child_restart` |
108	| ring | consumer stalls | sequence gap; late heartbeat | refuse and count (B.3); restart `storaged`; red | `ring_full`, `heartbeat_late` |
109	| storaged | power cut mid-write | bad CRC / no `COMMIT` at boot | truncate tail and open batch (D-025) | `recovered` |
110	| storaged | disk full; `fsync` or write `EIO` | `ENOSPC`, return values | drop oldest segment if allowed; hold durable offset; degrade, red | `enospc`, `fsync_failed` |
111	| analyzed | torn checkpoint; bad model file | slot CRC; header CRC | other slot + redo; residuals only | `checkpoint_bad`, `model_unavailable` |
112	| `statusd` | report fails, out of memory | error; RSS | page says so; capture unaffected | `report_failed` |
113	| supervisor | dies | systemd `Restart=always` | light freezes steady = "not running" | journal |
114	| clock | RTC lost backup (D-030) | invalid time at boot | run on `mono_ns`; wall time untrusted | `rtc_invalid` |
115	| power | key-off, cable pulled, crank dip, source back mid-shutdown | source-present GPIO timing | §6 state machine | `source_lost`, `source_dip`, `shutdown` |
116	| power | empty bank at cold crank | unclean end at next boot | crash recovery (D) | `recovered` |
117	| power, heat | undervoltage, throttling, charger live at key-off | `vcgencmd`, SoC temp | degrade, log, report; halt policy open | `undervoltage`, `thermal` |
118	| radio | BT and Wi-Fi share one chip | reply p99 in heartbeat | measure (`btcoex`) | heartbeat |
119	
120	## 5. Storage and data
121	
122	- **Format (D-034):** 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`, `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`,
123	  flags, `boot_id`), typed body, CRC32. Kinds: sample, begin, commit, boot, shutdown,
124	  event; a 56-byte sample keeps raw reply bytes beside the value. 16 MB segments, never
125	  edited.
126	- **Rates:** 10–25 samples/s is 0.56–1.4 KB/s, 2–5 MB per running hour.
127	- **Retention (D-041):** every segment is kept until the log filesystem is 80 % full,
128	  then whole segments go oldest first, never one the newest checkpoint still needs. A
129	  32 GB card holds years of two-hour days. Text logs go to the journal, size-capped.
130	- **fsync (D-035):** commit at 1 s or 64 samples, and at clean shutdown. An unclean cut
131	  loses at most a second of signals that move over minutes; longer batches lose warm-up
132	  at each cold-start reset; per-record `fsync` is 20× the flash wear.
133	- **Crash story:** at boot `storaged` scans from its last committed offset, verifies CRCs,
134	  truncates the torn tail and any uncommitted batch (undo is truncation: nothing is
135	  overwritten), and logs whether the last session ended clean. `analyzed` loads the newest
136	  valid checkpoint and redoes later batches through the live code path (D-025).
137	
138	## 6. The box: hardware and safe power-down
139	
140	One box: a Pi 4; one USB-C sink input (5 V only) from the owner's charger, with
141	protection, current and inrush limits; a supercapacitor bank (about 10 F, 105 J usable,
142	estimate) behind a 5 V / 3 A boost converter; an I2C clock (D-030); the DS18B20 on a lead
143	outside the shell (D-037); one tri-color light (D-027). **Source-present** tells the Pi
144	the charger is live; after **halt-done** the power stage cuts the Pi even if the source
145	has returned, then re-enables it (D-024). Nothing on the car is cut. Parts:
146	`hardware/BOM.md`; wiring: the schematic and `hardware/wiring.md`.
147	
148	| State | Entered when | Supervisor does | Light |
149	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
150	| `BOOTING` | power-on (~30 s, `bootbudget`) | start children, await heartbeats | steady yellow (hardware pull) |
151	| `RUNNING` | all healthy, source present | record | green pulse |
152	| `DEGRADED` | child down, dongle silent with engine on, storage or power fault | record what it can; log absent vs crashed | red blink |
153	| `GRACE` | source-present lost | keep recording; source back → `RUNNING` (a crank dip) | yellow blink |
154	| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | grace (~3 s) expires | stop `obdd`, final `COMMIT` + `fsync`, checkpoint, `sync`, halt; source back → finish, then reboot | yellow blink |
155	| `OFF` | halt-done; power stage cuts the Pi | nothing | dark |
156	
157	Energy (estimates, D-024): grace plus shutdown need 65–85 J of about 105 J usable. A
158	crash at any point is still recovered by mechanism D.
159	
160	> 🟨 **TEAM / LANCE (Wednesday):** the power block's parts, the bank size, the grace
161	> period and the shutdown time are estimates until `powerspec` and `capbench` measure
162	> them; replace each with a number or mark it "estimate". Decide what the box does when
163	> a charger stays live with the engine silent (`shutfsm`).
164	
165	## 7. Constraints and substitutions
166	
167	| Wanted | Using | Cost |
168	| --- | --- | --- |
169	| Every engine sensor | The Mode 01 PIDs the ECU publishes (D-022) | Oil pressure likely absent; lists differ by car |
170	| Outside air temperature | A DS18B20 in the cabin (D-037) | Reads cabin air: ambient only after a long soak, and sun-heated in summer |
171	| Failing engines | Induced, reversible faults on two healthy cars (D-021) | A few fault areas; no real wear-out |
172	| Raw CAN at ECU rate | Bluetooth Mode 01 request/response (D-019) | ~10–25 samples/s, no bus timing, a link that drops; most of the menu leaves the data path (D-017) |
173	| 48 continuous hours | 48 h of normal use across key cycles (D-023) | Sessions with gaps; the professor confirmed this reading (D-023) |
174	| Full hold-up | Owner's charger + seconds-scale supercapacitor (D-024) | A cold-start crank may reset the Pi |
175	| Recording from key-on | A ~30 s Pi 4 boot (`bootbudget`) | The first half-minute of warm-up is lost |
176	| The product on the first drives | A Python tool, labeled `live` (D-033) | Proves nothing about `obdd`; enters the product only as `replay` |
177	
178	## 8. Evaluation plan
179	
180	> 🟨 **TEAM:** these targets are D-036, a draft; agree each number or change it.
181	
182	| Measurement | Method | Target |
183	| --- | --- | --- |
184	| Reply → durable, p50 / p99 | timestamps at tty read and after `fsync`; idle and with a CPU hog | ≤ 1.2 s / ≤ 2.5 s |
185	| Sustained request rate | answers per second from the log, per drive | ≥ 10/s; every model input every ≤ 2 s |
186	| `kill -9` each child | 20 trials per child, from the log | detect ≤ 100 ms; heartbeat ≤ 5 s; no fd leak |
187	| Ring drops under contention (B.3) | sequence accounting, both rings | 0 |
188	| CPU per process | `utime` + `stime` in each heartbeat; idle and with a CPU hog | each daemon ≤ 10 % of one core; all ≤ 25 % |
189	| RSS over the soak | heartbeats at start, hourly, end, per session | slope < 100 KB per running hour |
190	| fsync batch size (`expbatch`) | per record, 1 s, 10 s on the Pi's SD: `fsync` p99, bytes written, loss per cut | 1 s: ≤ 1 s lost, ≤ ⅕ the bytes |
191	| Every failure-table row (§4) | inject each (EVALUATION.md §5) | its event logged; capture never stops for another's fault |
192	| Probe unplugged (D-037) | pull it with everything running | `sensor_absent` ≤ 10 s; engine capture unaffected |
193	| Detection per fault area | 5 induced events per area | ≥ 4 of 5; ≤ 1 false verdict per 10 h |
194	| Recovery after a cut mid-write | cut the Pi's 5 V rail after the converter | 50 / 50 recover; ≤ 1 batch lost |
195	| Boot to first durable sample | log time against the source-present edge | ≤ 45 s |
196

201	| Subsystem | Owner | Evidence |
202	| --- | --- | --- |

206	| `src/obd/`, `src/ambient/`, `src/analysis/`, `src/supervisor/`, `src/interface/`, `tools/train/`, `electricalDrawing/` | unclaimed | scaffolds only so far |
207

209	> still applies: the first substantive commit is the claim) and fill it in.

211	## 10. AI-use plan

# Design document — carwatch

> **WEDNESDAY REVIEW — delete this box, and every 🟨 / 📏 note, before submitting.**
> 🟨 **TEAM** = decide or review together. 📏 **DRIVE** = replace with a number from the
> first Forester drive (`firstcap`, `pidforester`). Checklist:
>
> - [ ] Sign, change or reject every review-queue entry this doc cites (`DECISIONS.md`).
> - [ ] Decide the fault-area rows in §3 and fill the ownership map in §9.
> - [ ] Drive numbers into §1, §3 and §5; Lance's power numbers into §6.
> - [ ] Three-isolated-workers check: design-only reader, BOM-only buyer, wiring-only
>   builder each succeed from their own part.
> - [ ] Render to PDF: 5 pages or fewer without this box.

**User and problem.** Lance drives a 2015 CR-V daily, and nothing reads his engine's
sensors except a check-engine light that speaks only once something has failed. carwatch
is a box that boots at every key-on, records every Mode 01 sensor through a Bluetooth
OBD2 dongle, learns *this* car's normal, and flags behavior that leaves it before the
light would. It is also tested on Camden's 2008 Forester (D-022). **Claim (D-021):** it
learns the normal of the car it is installed in, flags behavior outside it and names the
likely fault area, with measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.

## 1. Architecture

```text
OBD2 port -- OBDLink LX (Bluetooth SPP, D-019)   DS18B20 cabin probe (D-037)
   ~~ RFCOMM ~~> BlueZ -> rfcomm tty -> /dev/obd    1-Wire -> kernel w1-gpio -> sysfs
  obdd    Mode 01, one outstanding, ~10-25 req/s   ambientd   one read every 2 s
    | ring 1: SPSC, ~10-25 samples/s                  | ring 2: SPSC, 0.5 samples/s
    +------------------------+------------------------+  shared memory, refuse when full
                             v
  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
    v
  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
    v
  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,
    ^            1-4 Hz pulse = alive; steady, except yellow at boot = not running (D-027)
    | UDS, on demand
  obdctl (CLI); statusd: page + report --> phone on the box's Wi-Fi (D-013, D-043)
power: owner's USB-C charger -> power block + supercapacitor -> Pi 4 (D-024)
```

Rates are estimates until the first drive (`firstcap`); the logging tool reaches 22
requests a second on `obdsim`. One reply or probe reading is one sample, one record and
one analysis step. Queries go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the
answer (D-043); `analyzed` never reads a ring (D-031).

> 📏 **DRIVE:** measured request rate, reply-time p50/p99 and PID count replace the
> estimates here and in §5.

## 2. Mechanism mapping

D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: these rates never stress
a ring, and 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to us (D-029, D-037).

| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold crank, pulled cable; D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cuts of the Pi's 5 V rail mid-write; records lost per cut |
| E | `supervisor`, `src/ipc/` | A recorder that dies silently harms an owner who thinks it is on duty. Analysis, the least trusted code, must not take capture or storage down (B.2), and each sensor source has its own process, so a hung link cannot stop the probe (D-037) | `kill -9` each child 20×: detection, recovery, fd leaks |

**Two distinct sensors that cooperate (handout §3.1).** The DS18B20 and the car's
coolant and intake-air sensors are different devices on different buses, read by
different processes (D-037). After hours off (the clock says how long, D-030) all three
should agree at key-on; the one that disagrees is the suspect. The engine's own sensors
are distinct transducers the dongle only carries, and every diagnostic fuses at least two
(D.4). "Both sensors alive" (M2) is a real Mode 01 capture plus a probe reading; "through
the pipeline" (M3) is both as committed records labeled `live`.

## 3. Analysis: how normal is learned and a fault area named

All our code (handout §3.3; D.1, D.2). Per committed sample, `analyzed` (1) bins by
rpm × load × coolant temperature, so a cold idle is never compared with a warm cruise;
(2) keeps per-bin running mean and covariance (Welford), in A/B checkpoints; (3) scores the
Mahalanobis distance from the bin's baseline, which fires when a *partnership* breaks;
(4) fits Theil–Sen slopes of residuals across drives; (5) names the area with our
classifier (trained in `tools/train/`, inference in C; without weights, 1–4 still flag);
(6) surfaces verdicts through a hysteresis-and-dwell state machine (D.3).

| Fault area (D-021) | Cooperating sensors | Signature | Induced by (E.2) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Cooling | coolant, intake temp, ambient (PID 0x46, else the probe), load, speed | warm-up slope or warm settling temperature off its bin's normal for the same ambient and load | cardboard over the radiator |
| Air/fuel | fuel trims, MAP or MAF, rpm, O2 | long-term trim rising at idle with idle MAP, shrinking with load | a small vacuum line opened |
| Sensor/electrical | the failed PID and its usual partners; module voltage; at a cold start, coolant, intake temp and the probe | one PID absent or flat while its partners move; after a long soak, one temperature off the other two | a sensor unplugged |
| Unknown | all | residual high, no area matches | — |

No row can be called by one threshold on one value: each compares sensors that normally
move together, inside one bin (D.4). 📏 **DRIVE:** strike any sensor the survey shows the
Forester does not publish.

> 🟨 **TEAM DECIDES (Wednesday):** the fault-area rows, signatures and bin axes above are
> Claude's draft from D-021 and D.2 (§10). Confirm, change or replace each row, and then
> delete this note.

## 4. Failure-mode table

Log lines are `<process> <level> <event> key=value` with `src`; the table names the event.

| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log event |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| adapter | Bluetooth drops | `read` 0/`EIO`, `POLLHUP` | reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff | `link_lost`, `reconnected` |
| adapter | garbage or timeouts | parse failure; timeout | 3 in a row: `ATZ`, then reopen | `reply_bad`, `adapter_reset` |
| adapter | engine off, key in ACC | `0100` gets `NO DATA` | poll `0100` every few s, record nothing | `ecu_silent` |
| ECU | a sensor unplugged or failed | 5 `NO DATA` in a row; or pinned or flat while its partners move, MIL on (PID 0101) | mark absent or suspect, retry each minute. ECUs often substitute a value and light the CEL: not caught before the light | `pid_absent`, `pid_flat`, `mil_on`, `pid_present` |
| probe | unplugged, broken wire, bad read | device gone from sysfs; CRC `NO`; the 85.0 °C power-on value | mark absent, retry every 10 s; cold-soak check off, reported | `sensor_absent`, `sensor_present`, `reply_bad` |
| any child | crash, `kill -9` | `waitpid` | restart with backoff; others run on | `child_exit`, `child_restart` |
| ring | consumer stalls | sequence gap; late heartbeat | refuse and count (B.3); restart `storaged`; red | `ring_full`, `heartbeat_late` |
| storaged | power cut mid-write | bad CRC / no `COMMIT` at boot | truncate tail and open batch (D-025) | `recovered` |
| storaged | disk full; `fsync` or write `EIO` | `ENOSPC`, return values | drop oldest segment if allowed; hold durable offset; degrade, red | `enospc`, `fsync_failed` |
| analyzed | torn checkpoint; bad model file | slot CRC; header CRC | other slot + redo; residuals only | `checkpoint_bad`, `model_unavailable` |
| `statusd` | report fails, out of memory | error; RSS | page says so; capture unaffected | `report_failed` |
| supervisor | dies | systemd `Restart=always` | light freezes steady = "not running" | journal |
| clock | RTC lost backup (D-030) | invalid time at boot | run on `mono_ns`; wall time untrusted | `rtc_invalid` |
| power | key-off, cable pulled, crank dip, source back mid-shutdown | source-present GPIO timing | §6 state machine | `source_lost`, `source_dip`, `shutdown` |
| power | empty bank at cold crank | unclean end at next boot | crash recovery (D) | `recovered` |
| power, heat | undervoltage, throttling, charger live at key-off | `vcgencmd`, SoC temp | degrade, log, report; halt policy open | `undervoltage`, `thermal` |
| radio | BT and Wi-Fi share one chip | reply p99 in heartbeat | measure (`btcoex`) | heartbeat |

## 5. Storage and data

- **Format (D-034):** 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`, `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`,

  edited.
- **Rates:** 10–25 samples/s is 0.56–1.4 KB/s, 2–5 MB per running hour.
- **Retention (D-041):** every segment is kept until the log filesystem is 80 % full,
  then whole segments go oldest first, never one the newest checkpoint still needs. A
  32 GB card holds years of two-hour days. Text logs go to the journal, size-capped.
- **fsync (D-035):** commit at 1 s or 64 samples, and at clean shutdown. An unclean cut
  loses at most a second of signals that move over minutes; longer batches lose warm-up

- **Crash story:** at boot `storaged` scans from its last committed offset, verifies CRCs,
  truncates the torn tail and any uncommitted batch (undo is truncation: nothing is
  overwritten), and logs whether the last session ended clean. `analyzed` loads the newest
  valid checkpoint and redoes later batches through the live code path (D-025).

## 6. The box: hardware and safe power-down

outside the shell (D-037); one tri-color light (D-027). **Source-present** tells the Pi
the charger is live; after **halt-done** the power stage cuts the Pi even if the source
has returned, then re-enables it (D-024). Nothing on the car is cut. Parts:
`hardware/BOM.md`; wiring: the schematic and `hardware/wiring.md`.

| State | Entered when | Supervisor does | Light |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `BOOTING` | power-on (~30 s, `bootbudget`) | start children, await heartbeats | steady yellow (hardware pull) |
| `RUNNING` | all healthy, source present | record | green pulse |
| `DEGRADED` | child down, dongle silent with engine on, storage or power fault | record what it can; log absent vs crashed | red blink |
| `GRACE` | source-present lost | keep recording; source back → `RUNNING` (a crank dip) | yellow blink |
| `SHUTTING_DOWN` | grace (~3 s) expires | stop `obdd`, final `COMMIT` + `fsync`, checkpoint, `sync`, halt; source back → finish, then reboot | yellow blink |
| `OFF` | halt-done; power stage cuts the Pi | nothing | dark |

Energy (estimates, D-024): grace plus shutdown need 65–85 J of about 105 J usable. A
crash at any point is still recovered by mechanism D.

> 🟨 **TEAM / LANCE (Wednesday):** the power block's parts, the bank size, the grace
> period and the shutdown time are estimates until `powerspec` and `capbench` measure
> them; replace each with a number or mark it "estimate". Decide what the box does when
> a charger stays live with the engine silent (`shutfsm`).

# Decision log — carwatch

**Purpose:** every design decision on this project, in one place, organized by category so
you can find what you need without knowing an ID. This is an **audit log**, not a
reference doc — its job is to let Camden and Lance verify, after any working session,
that no decision was made on their behalf that they disagree with.

**This file holds what is DECIDED. Open work and open questions live on the board**,
`docs/milestones.md`, mirrored to GitHub issues, with no pre-assigned owners (D-020, D-026,
`CLAUDE.md` §7.11).
An ❓ OPEN entry below exists only as a pointer to its issue, so the reasoning sits beside
the decisions it will eventually join.

## How to use this file

**After every Claude Code session, read the Review Queue below.** It lists every
decision that no human has signed off on yet. That is the whole point of this file.

**After your partner's session, skim the Review Queue too.** Their agent's choices bind
your subsystems as surely as yours do.

## Status legend

| Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- |

## A. Hardware and interfaces

### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter; USB is the fallback ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-019` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-015 (§G.4)

*Pi power revised 2026-10-21 by D-024 (§A.6), before any review: the Pi is in a box fed
by the owner's USB-C charger, not wired to the car's USB. The adapter's key-off draw is
now board item `dongledrain`.*

**Decision.** An **OBDLink LX** (STN chip, **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile**; not
BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, in the box (D-024), talks to it with
its built-in Bluetooth radio over RFCOMM. Provisioning pairs and trusts the adapter once,
binds it with `rfcomm bind` to `/dev/rfcomm0`, and a udev rule links that to **`/dev/obd`**,
so every consumer still opens `/dev/obd` and sends Mode 01 requests (D-012). No MCP2515, no
SPI, no CAN wiring, and no data cable in the cabin.

**Raw CAN is still a stretch goal**: an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D
and E are implemented *and measured* (unchanged from D-015).

**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23: the goal is the simplest data path that works. The box
becomes one power cable; the adapter stays in the port. The protocol, the parsing and every
downstream design are the same as D-015, because an STN adapter speaks the same ELM327
command set over Bluetooth as over USB.

*Note 2026-10-27: D-038 rewrote `make boundary`. `AF_BLUETOOTH` is now banned everywhere,
and Unix sockets are allowed through `src/ipc/uds.c`, so the reasoning below still holds.*

**Why a tty and not our own Bluetooth socket.** Opening an RFCOMM socket from `obdd` would
put `socket()` in `src/obd/`, which `make boundary` forbids outside `src/interface/`
(CLAUDE.md §2.1). Letting the kernel's RFCOMM layer present a tty keeps the boundary check
meaningful and keeps `obdd` a plain serial reader.

**What D-001 (§G.1) said against this, and why it no longer applies.** G.1 rejected a
Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up interrupts and bus-level timing, taking mechanisms A,
B, C and F with it. D-015 already accepted exactly that loss for the USB adapter, and D-017
records what survives (D and E). Bluetooth costs no further mechanism.

**Costs and risks.**

- **Provisioning.** Pairing, trust and a persistent bind must survive reboots and every
  key-off (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`, board item `bench`).
- **A new failure mode.** The link can drop while the engine runs (adapter out of range,
  adapter asleep, radio interference). `obdd` sees a hangup on the tty and must reconnect
  with backoff, not crash-loop (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4, `supbackoff`).
- **One radio, two jobs.** The Pi 4's single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs the phone
  access point (D-013). Coexistence is expected to work but is unmeasured: board item
  `btcoex`. Putting the access point on 5 GHz is the first mitigation to try.
- **Key-off draw.** The adapter still draws from OBD2 pin 16, live with the key off, and a
  Bluetooth adapter keeps a radio up. Its sleep behavior and key-off current are measured
  before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).

**Fallback.** The USB adapter of D-015 (§G.4) needs only a different udev rule to appear as
`/dev/obd`. If Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car, switching back is a provisioning
change, not a code change.

1	# Design document — carwatch
2	
3	> **WEDNESDAY REVIEW — delete this box, and every 🟨 / 📏 note, before submitting.**
4	> 🟨 **TEAM** = decide or review together. 📏 **DRIVE** = replace with a number from the
5	> first Forester drive (`firstcap`, `pidforester`). Checklist:
6	>
7	> - [ ] Sign, change or reject every review-queue entry this doc cites (`DECISIONS.md`).
8	> - [ ] Decide the fault-area rows in §3 and fill the ownership map in §9.
9	> - [ ] Drive numbers into §1, §3 and §5; Lance's power numbers into §6.
10	> - [ ] Three-isolated-workers check: design-only reader, BOM-only buyer, wiring-only
11	>   builder each succeed from their own part.
12	> - [ ] Render to PDF: 5 pages or fewer without this box.
13	
14	**User and problem.** Lance drives a 2015 CR-V daily, and nothing reads his engine's
15	sensors except a check-engine light that speaks only once something has failed. carwatch
16	is a box that boots at every key-on, records every Mode 01 sensor through a Bluetooth
17	OBD2 dongle, learns *this* car's normal, and flags behavior that leaves it before the
18	light would. It is also tested on Camden's 2008 Forester (D-022). **Claim (D-021):** it
19	learns the normal of the car it is installed in, flags behavior outside it and names the
20	likely fault area, with measured catch and false-alarm rates on faults we induce.
21	
22	## 1. Architecture
23	
24	```text
25	OBD2 port -- OBDLink LX (Bluetooth SPP, D-019)   DS18B20 cabin probe (D-037)
26	   ~~ RFCOMM ~~> BlueZ -> rfcomm tty -> /dev/obd    1-Wire -> kernel w1-gpio -> sysfs
27	  obdd    Mode 01, one outstanding, ~10-25 req/s   ambientd   one read every 2 s
28	    | ring 1: SPSC, ~10-25 samples/s                  | ring 2: SPSC, 0.5 samples/s
29	    +------------------------+------------------------+  shared memory, refuse when full
30	                             v
31	  storaged [D]  BEGIN..COMMIT batches, 1 fsync/s, ~1 KB/s -> ext4 on SD (D-025)
32	    ^           events from every daemon: one SEQPACKET Unix socket, a few a drive (D-042)
33	    | committed records only, read back from the log, ~1 s behind (D-031)
34	    v
35	  analyzed      bins -> baselines -> residuals -> trends -> model -> FSM
36	    | verdicts over a Unix socket, a few per drive at most
37	    v
38	  supervisor [E] spawns, heartbeats, restarts with backoff --GPIO--> light,
39	    ^            1-4 Hz pulse = alive; steady, except yellow at boot = not running (D-027)
40	    | UDS, on demand
41	  obdctl (CLI); statusd: page + report --> phone on the box's Wi-Fi (D-013, D-043)
42	power: owner's USB-C charger -> power block + supercapacitor -> Pi 4 (D-024)
43	```
44	
45	Rates are estimates until the first drive (`firstcap`); the logging tool reaches 22
46	requests a second on `obdsim`. One reply or probe reading is one sample, one record and
47	one analysis step. Queries go to the supervisor, which asks the process holding the
48	answer (D-043); `analyzed` never reads a ring (D-031).
49	
50	> 📏 **DRIVE:** measured request rate, reply-time p50/p99 and PID count replace the
51	> estimates here and in §5.
52	
53	## 2. Mechanism mapping
54	
55	D and E are the committed pair (D-017). B and F stay declined: these rates never stress
56	a ring, and 1-Wire timing belongs to the kernel, not to us (D-029, D-037).
57	
58	| Item | Component | Justification from the user's requirements | Measured by |
59	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
60	| D | `storaged`; checkpoints in `analyzed` | Power can vanish at any instant (empty bank at a cold crank, pulled cable; D-024), yet the record and weeks of learned baselines must survive, and no baseline may learn a sample a cut later erased (D-031): append-only CRC'd records, 1 s commits, A/B checkpoints (D-025, D-035) | 50 cuts of the Pi's 5 V rail mid-write; records lost per cut |
61	| E | `supervisor`, `src/ipc/` | A recorder that dies silently harms an owner who thinks it is on duty. Analysis, the least trusted code, must not take capture or storage down (B.2), and each sensor source has its own process, so a hung link cannot stop the probe (D-037) | `kill -9` each child 20×: detection, recovery, fd leaks |
62	
63	**Two distinct sensors that cooperate (handout §3.1).** The DS18B20 and the car's
64	coolant and intake-air sensors are different devices on different buses, read by
65	different processes (D-037). After hours off (the clock says how long, D-030) all three
66	should agree at key-on; the one that disagrees is the suspect. The engine's own sensors
67	are distinct transducers the dongle only carries, and every diagnostic fuses at least two
68	(D.4). "Both sensors alive" (M2) is a real Mode 01 capture plus a probe reading; "through
69	the pipeline" (M3) is both as committed records labeled `live`.
70	
71	## 3. Analysis: how normal is learned and a fault area named
72	
73	All our code (handout §3.3; D.1, D.2). Per committed sample, `analyzed` (1) bins by
74	rpm × load × coolant temperature, so a cold idle is never compared with a warm cruise;
75	(2) keeps per-bin running mean and covariance (Welford), in A/B checkpoints; (3) scores the
76	Mahalanobis distance from the bin's baseline, which fires when a *partnership* breaks;
77	(4) fits Theil–Sen slopes of residuals across drives; (5) names the area with our
78	classifier (trained in `tools/train/`, inference in C; without weights, 1–4 still flag);
79	(6) surfaces verdicts through a hysteresis-and-dwell state machine (D.3).
80	
81	| Fault area (D-021) | Cooperating sensors | Signature | Induced by (E.2) |
82	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
83	| Cooling | coolant, intake temp, ambient (PID 0x46, else the probe), load, speed | warm-up slope or warm settling temperature off its bin's normal for the same ambient and load | cardboard over the radiator |
84	| Air/fuel | fuel trims, MAP or MAF, rpm, O2 | long-term trim rising at idle with idle MAP, shrinking with load | a small vacuum line opened |
85	| Sensor/electrical | the failed PID and its usual partners; module voltage; at a cold start, coolant, intake temp and the probe | one PID absent or flat while its partners move; after a long soak, one temperature off the other two | a sensor unplugged |
86	| Unknown | all | residual high, no area matches | — |
87	
88	No row can be called by one threshold on one value: each compares sensors that normally
89	move together, inside one bin (D.4). 📏 **DRIVE:** strike any sensor the survey shows the
90	Forester does not publish.
91	
92	> 🟨 **TEAM DECIDES (Wednesday):** the fault-area rows, signatures and bin axes above are
93	> Claude's draft from D-021 and D.2 (§10). Confirm, change or replace each row, and then
94	> delete this note.
95	
96	## 4. Failure-mode table
97	
98	Log lines are `<process> <level> <event> key=value` with `src`; the table names the event.
99	
100	| Component | Failure | Detection | Response | Log event |
101	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
102	| adapter | Bluetooth drops | `read` 0/`EIO`, `POLLHUP` | reopen `/dev/obd` with backoff | `link_lost`, `reconnected` |
103	| adapter | garbage or timeouts | parse failure; timeout | 3 in a row: `ATZ`, then reopen | `reply_bad`, `adapter_reset` |
104	| adapter | engine off, key in ACC | `0100` gets `NO DATA` | poll `0100` every few s, record nothing | `ecu_silent` |
105	| ECU | a sensor unplugged or failed | 5 `NO DATA` in a row; or pinned or flat while its partners move, MIL on (PID 0101) | mark absent or suspect, retry each minute. ECUs often substitute a value and light the CEL: not caught before the light | `pid_absent`, `pid_flat`, `mil_on`, `pid_present` |
106	| probe | unplugged, broken wire, bad read | device gone from sysfs; CRC `NO`; the 85.0 °C power-on value | mark absent, retry every 10 s; cold-soak check off, reported | `sensor_absent`, `sensor_present`, `reply_bad` |
107	| any child | crash, `kill -9` | `waitpid` | restart with backoff; others run on | `child_exit`, `child_restart` |
108	| ring | consumer stalls | sequence gap; late heartbeat | refuse and count (B.3); restart `storaged`; red | `ring_full`, `heartbeat_late` |
109	| storaged | power cut mid-write | bad CRC / no `COMMIT` at boot | truncate tail and open batch (D-025) | `recovered` |
110	| storaged | disk full; `fsync` or write `EIO` | `ENOSPC`, return values | drop oldest segment if allowed; hold durable offset; degrade, red | `enospc`, `fsync_failed` |
111	| analyzed | torn checkpoint; bad model file | slot CRC; header CRC | other slot + redo; residuals only | `checkpoint_bad`, `model_unavailable` |
112	| `statusd` | report fails, out of memory | error; RSS | page says so; capture unaffected | `report_failed` |
113	| supervisor | dies | systemd `Restart=always` | light freezes steady = "not running" | journal |
114	| clock | RTC lost backup (D-030) | invalid time at boot | run on `mono_ns`; wall time untrusted | `rtc_invalid` |
115	| power | key-off, cable pulled, crank dip, source back mid-shutdown | source-present GPIO timing | §6 state machine | `source_lost`, `source_dip`, `shutdown` |
116	| power | empty bank at cold crank | unclean end at next boot | crash recovery (D) | `recovered` |
117	| power, heat | undervoltage, throttling, charger live at key-off | `vcgencmd`, SoC temp | degrade, log, report; halt policy open | `undervoltage`, `thermal` |
118	| radio | BT and Wi-Fi share one chip | reply p99 in heartbeat | measure (`btcoex`) | heartbeat |
119	
120	## 5. Storage and data
121	
122	- **Format (D-034):** 40-byte header (`magic`, `kind`, `seq`, `mono_ns`, `wall_ns`, `src`,
123	  flags, `boot_id`), typed body, CRC32. Kinds: sample, begin, commit, boot, shutdown,
124	  event; a 56-byte sample keeps raw reply bytes beside the value. 16 MB segments, never
125	  edited.
126	- **Rates:** 10–25 samples/s is 0.56–1.4 KB/s, 2–5 MB per running hour.
127	- **Retention (D-041):** every segment is kept until the log filesystem is 80 % full,
128	  then whole segments go oldest first, never one the newest checkpoint still needs. A
129	  32 GB card holds years of two-hour days. Text logs go to the journal, size-capped.
130	- **fsync (D-035):** commit at 1 s or 64 samples, and at clean shutdown. An unclean cut
131	  loses at most a second of signals that move over minutes; longer batches lose warm-up
132	  at each cold-start reset; per-record `fsync` is 20× the flash wear.
133	- **Crash story:** at boot `storaged` scans from its last committed offset, verifies CRCs,
134	  truncates the torn tail and any uncommitted batch (undo is truncation: nothing is
135	  overwritten), and logs whether the last session ended clean. `analyzed` loads the newest
136	  valid checkpoint and redoes later batches through the live code path (D-025).

140	One box: a Pi 4; one USB-C sink input (5 V only) from the owner's charger, with

## A. Hardware and interfaces

### A.1 — The Pi reads OBD2 over a Bluetooth Classic adapter; USB is the fallback ⚠️ UNREVIEWED

`D-019` · Decided M1, 2026-09-23 · **By:** Camden (in session) + Claude
· **Reviewed:** Camden ⬜ / Lance ⬜
· **Supersedes:** D-015 (§G.4)

*Pi power revised 2026-10-21 by D-024 (§A.6), before any review: the Pi is in a box fed
by the owner's USB-C charger, not wired to the car's USB. The adapter's key-off draw is
now board item `dongledrain`.*

**Decision.** An **OBDLink LX** (STN chip, **Bluetooth Classic, Serial Port Profile**; not
BLE) plugs into the OBD2 port. The Pi, in the box (D-024), talks to it with
its built-in Bluetooth radio over RFCOMM. Provisioning pairs and trusts the adapter once,
binds it with `rfcomm bind` to `/dev/rfcomm0`, and a udev rule links that to **`/dev/obd`**,
so every consumer still opens `/dev/obd` and sends Mode 01 requests (D-012). No MCP2515, no
SPI, no CAN wiring, and no data cable in the cabin.

**Raw CAN is still a stretch goal**: an MCP2515 on SPI, taken up only after mechanisms D
and E are implemented *and measured* (unchanged from D-015).

**Why.** Camden's call, 2026-09-23: the goal is the simplest data path that works. The box
becomes one power cable; the adapter stays in the port. The protocol, the parsing and every
downstream design are the same as D-015, because an STN adapter speaks the same ELM327
command set over Bluetooth as over USB.

*Note 2026-10-27: D-038 rewrote `make boundary`. `AF_BLUETOOTH` is now banned everywhere,
and Unix sockets are allowed through `src/ipc/uds.c`, so the reasoning below still holds.*

**Why a tty and not our own Bluetooth socket.** Opening an RFCOMM socket from `obdd` would
put `socket()` in `src/obd/`, which `make boundary` forbids outside `src/interface/`
(CLAUDE.md §2.1). Letting the kernel's RFCOMM layer present a tty keeps the boundary check
meaningful and keeps `obdd` a plain serial reader.

**What D-001 (§G.1) said against this, and why it no longer applies.** G.1 rejected a
Bluetooth ELM327 because it gives up interrupts and bus-level timing, taking mechanisms A,
B, C and F with it. D-015 already accepted exactly that loss for the USB adapter, and D-017
records what survives (D and E). Bluetooth costs no further mechanism.

**Costs and risks.**

- **Provisioning.** Pairing, trust and a persistent bind must survive reboots and every
  key-off (`scripts/provision_pi.sh`, board item `bench`).
- **A new failure mode.** The link can drop while the engine runs (adapter out of range,
  adapter asleep, radio interference). `obdd` sees a hangup on the tty and must reconnect
  with backoff, not crash-loop (`docs/DESIGN.md` §4, `supbackoff`).
- **One radio, two jobs.** The Pi 4's single Wi-Fi/Bluetooth chip also runs the phone
  access point (D-013). Coexistence is expected to work but is unmeasured: board item
  `btcoex`. Putting the access point on 5 GHz is the first mitigation to try.
- **Key-off draw.** The adapter still draws from OBD2 pin 16, live with the key off, and a
  Bluetooth adapter keeps a radio up. Its sleep behavior and key-off current are measured
  before it stays plugged in overnight (`dongledrain`).

**Fallback.** The USB adapter of D-015 (§G.4) needs only a different udev rule to appear as
`/dev/obd`. If Bluetooth proves unreliable in the car, switching back is a provisioning
change, not a code change.

309-
310-The user is an adult child who lives an hour, or a continent, away from a parent who lives
311-alone. The moment the product exists for is a quiet one: not the fall, but the morning that
312-didn't follow its rhythm, noticed hours before anyone would have been frightened enough to
313-call. Every existing answer asks the parent to *do* something. Wear the pendant. Charge the
314-watch. Answer the daily check-in. And the failure mode is that the people most at risk are
315-precisely the people least likely to keep doing it. The design brief is then a device that
316-demands nothing: no camera, no microphone, no button, no new habit. That restraint is not a
317-limitation to apologize for. It's the product's spine, and a memo that can articulate why a
318-motion sensor is more respectful than a camera is a memo that understands its user.
319-
320-**Engineering:** a PIR motion sensor and a door or pressure sensor, learning a household's
321-rhythm. The intelligence (all of it yours) is per-hour activity histograms over a rolling
322-window of weeks, a deviation score that knows a Tuesday from a Sunday, and alert hysteresis.
323-Because the real analytical problem here isn't detection. It's restraint. A monitor that
324-cries wolf twice gets unplugged. An unplugged monitor is worse than none, because somebody
325-far away believes it's on duty. Natural mechanisms: **E**, because a silently dead wellness
326-monitor is this product's own nightmare scenario, which makes process isolation and
327-supervision requirements rather than garnish; and **D**, because weeks of learned baseline
328-must survive a power cut. A scoped-down version that still clears every bar: one room, one
329-rhythm, two weeks of baseline, and an alert log you evaluate for false-alarm rate. No paging
330-infrastructure required.
331-

446-  RMS level is a serviceable occupancy proxy. And two cheap sensors that corroborate each
447-  other routinely outperform one expensive one standing alone. Notice that "corroborate each
448:  other" is Section 3.1 arriving early, wearing a budget. Record in the design document what
449-  you wanted, what you used, and what the substitution costs in capability.
450-
451-- **Make your own ground truth.** You can't wait for the bearing to fail, so you provoke the
452-  conditions and label the recordings: the taped washer, the loosened bolt, the greenhouse
453-  vent propped open on purpose, a one-week paper logbook of real door events. **Ten labeled
454-  recordings you made are worth more than ten thousand unlabeled samples you found**,
455-  because you know what yours mean. And at the defense, you will be asked how you know.

content.content:
## 8. The Design Document (M2)

**3–5 pages** and the most leveraged hours of the whole project. Because every hour of
arguing here saves five of rewriting later. Required contents:

- **Architecture.** A diagram in the spirit of Figure 1: processes, threads, kernel
  components, data flows, and **rates on every arrow**.
- **Mechanism mapping.** For each chosen menu item: which component implements it, and a
  justification from the user's requirements (*"the vibration analysis is meaningless above
  2 ms of sampling jitter, hence `SCHED_FIFO`"*).
- **Failure-mode table.** For each component: how it can fail, how the failure is detected,
  what the system does about it, and what the log will show. The soak test (Section 3.4)
  will grade this table's honesty.
- **Storage and data.** What is stored, at what rate, in what format, with what retention,
  and what happens to it when the power dies mid-write.
- **Constraints and substitutions.** What the ideal build would use, what you're actually
  using, and what the gap costs: sensors downgraded, data synthesized or replayed, claims
  narrowed (Section 5). *A design document with nothing to report here has usually not met
  its hardware yet.*
- **Evaluation plan.** The measurements you will take (Section 9), each with its method and
  its target. Numbers you commit to now are twice as credible when you hit them later. And
  instructive either way.
- **Ownership map.** Which partner owns which subsystems (Section 10.1). Ownership means
  first authorship and answerability at the defense, not exclusivity.
- **AI-use plan.** What you'll use Claude Code for, what you won't, and how you'll keep the
  Section 3.3 boundary visible in your repository (e.g., the product source tree contains no
  network client but the LAN interface).

---

## 9. The Evaluation Report (M5)
## 6. Milestones

The project runs from Week 3 through demo week. Milestones are due at the end of the listed
week; each is graded, and each exists to make a specific late-semester disaster impossible.

| Milestone | Deliverable | Week | Est. team hours |
|---|---|---|---|
| **M0** | Team formed; hardware ordered; repo and `CLAUDE.md` initialized | 4 | 2–3 |
| **M1** | Problem memo (Section 7); each partner's `.jsonl` transcripts to date copied out | 5 | 3–4 |
| **M2** | Design document (Section 8); both sensors electrically alive; transcripts copied out | 7 | 8–10 |
| **M3** | Checkpoint demo: both sensors flowing through the real pipeline into real storage; at least one menu mechanism working; transcripts copied out | 10 | 25–30 |
| **M4** | Feature freeze; 48-hour soak begins; transcripts copied out | 14 | 30–40 |
| **M5** | Final submission: system, soak logs, evaluation report, process artifacts, complete transcripts | 15 | 10–14 |
| **M6** | Demo day: live demonstration, fault injection, individual defenses | 15–16 | n/a |

**Transcript submission is not a one-time, end-of-semester task.** At every milestone from
M1 through M5, each partner copies out their raw `.jsonl` Claude Code session files
(Section 10) covering the work done since the previous milestone. Building this habit in
Week 5 is the point: it costs a minute per milestone, and it is the only way to guarantee
that the transcripts graded at M5 actually cover the whole semester rather than whatever the
local 30-day retention window happened to spare.

The disasters, in order: a team that never quite forms; a project nobody wants; a design
that was never written down and so was never argued about; an integration that begins the
night before it is graded; a soak test that can't start because the system can't yet run for
an hour; a demo that meets its first unplugged sensor in front of an audience; and Week-5
transcripts that no longer exist by Week 15 because nobody copied them out along the way.

---

# Supported-PID survey

**Sets the model's input list (D-021, D-022). Run it on each car's first drive.**

Method: `tools/pidscan.py`, as `docs/hardware/first-drive.md` describes (Mac or Pi). It
sends `ATZ`, `ATE0`, `ATSP0`, then the supported-PID bitmaps `0100`, `0120`, `0140`, ...
(each a 32-bit map of which PIDs in the next block the ECU answers), takes one reading of
every supported PID, and writes a markdown block for this file. Paste that block and the
raw replies below the table, dated. By hand, the same commands work in `screen /dev/obd`.

## What we specifically need to know

Vehicles (D-022): Camden's **2008 Subaru Forester** (non-turbo; OBD protocol not yet
verified, expected CAN) and Lance's **2015 Honda CR-V EX-L** (D-007; engine and
transmission still to be confirmed from the VIN). For each car, also record the protocol
the adapter negotiated (`ATDP`) and the VIN's hash, which is what `pidscan` stores (D-033);
whether this file also records the raw VIN is open (`vinsurvey`).

| PID | Signal | Forester | CR-V | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0x01 | Monitor status: MIL and DTC count | | | the failure table's `mil_on` |
| 0x0C | RPM | | | bin axis |
| 0x04 | Calculated load | | | bin axis |
| 0x05 | Coolant temp | | | bin axis; cooling; cold-soak check |
| 0x0F | Intake air temp | | | cold-soak check |
| 0x46 | Ambient air temp | | | cooling; else the DS18B20 (D-037) |
| 0x0D | Vehicle speed | | | cooling |
| 0x0B | MAP | | | air/fuel |
| 0x10 | MAF | | | air/fuel, if MAP is absent |
| 0x11 | Throttle position | | | |
| 0x06 | Short-term fuel trim B1 | | | air/fuel |
| 0x07 | Long-term fuel trim B1 | | | air/fuel |
| 0x14–0x1B | O2 sensor voltages | | | air/fuel |
| 0x42 | Control module voltage | | | sensor/electrical |
| 0x5C | Engine oil temp | | | |
| — | Oil pressure | | | Usually not a standard PID; the CR-V likely has only a switch. Nothing depends on it (D-021). |
| 0x2F | Fuel level | | | |
| 0x31 | Distance since codes cleared | | | odometer proxy |

raw replies below the table, dated. By hand, the same commands work in `screen /dev/obd`.

## What you've done (about 280 commits; Lance has 4)

- **M0–M1:** You set up the repo, `CLAUDE.md`, the build and the board (`milestones.md` synced to GitHub issues), and wrote `PROBLEM.md`. You moved to a Bluetooth OBDLink LX (D-019) and reframed the project as a one-car monitor that names the fault area (D-021).

  - Tightened the network-boundary check (D-038).
  - Added Linux CI and fixed the sanitizer build.
  - Fixed bugs in the logging tools (D-044).
  - Wrote the storage code: shared-memory rings that free slots only after `fsync` (D-039), the record format and its checksum, crash recovery, and a storage daemon that loses nothing when killed. This is most of mechanism D, plus the lossless-restart part of E.

## The product, in one breath

A Pi 4 in a small USB-C box. It boots at key-on and reads every engine sensor the car publishes through a Bluetooth OBD2 dongle, plus a cabin temperature probe. It learns *this* car's normal for each operating point (rpm × load × coolant temperature), flags sensors that stop moving together, and names the likely fault area: cooling, air/fuel, or sensor/electrical. The owner reads it on a phone over the box's own Wi-Fi. There's no cloud and no network. What you're graded on is mechanisms D (crash-safe storage) and E (separate processes under a supervisor).

# First drive: survey and log the Forester

**Feeds:** `pidforester`, `firstcap`, `baseline` (M2). **Tools:** `tools/pidscan.py`,
`tools/obdlog.py` (D-033). **Adapter:** OBDLink LX (D-019).

The adapter takes its power from the car's OBD2 port (pin 16), so none of this works at a
desk. Everything below has been rehearsed against `obdsim`; the first real run is the
only unknown, so expect the port name and the timing to need a look.

## Before leaving the house

1. Set up the tools once (needs the network):

   ```sh
   make toolcheck          # builds .venv (pyserial, matplotlib) and runs the tool tests
   ```

2. Rehearse the whole path against the simulator:

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py --sim --max-seconds 20
   ```

   It should report about 20 samples per second and write
   `data/drive-<time>-synth.jsonl`.
3. Charge the laptop. Optional: `pip install -r tools/requirements-gps.txt` into the
   venv for `--gps`, then run the rehearsal once with `--gps` so macOS asks for the
   location permission at the desk, not in the car.
4. Turn off sleep for the drive: run the logger under `caffeinate -i` (below), and keep
   the lid open. `caffeinate -i` does not stop the sleep a closed lid causes on battery.

## In the car, parked (about 10 minutes)

1. Plug the LX into the OBD2 port, under the dash on the driver's side. Start the engine.
2. Pair it: System Settings, Bluetooth. If it does not show up, check the quick-start
   card in the box for how the LX enters pairing mode.
3. Find its serial port:

   ```sh
   ls /dev/cu.*
   ```

   Record the name here. If no new `/dev/cu.*` appears after pairing, the Mac route has
   failed: use the Pi (last section).
4. Survey, engine idling:

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/pidscan.py --port /dev/cu.<name>
   ```

   It prints the protocol, the battery voltage, the VIN (on screen only) and one reading
   per supported PID, and writes `data/pidscan-<time>-live.{json,md}`. If it hangs at
   the start, the adapter is still searching for the protocol; give it 15 s.

## The drive

```sh
caffeinate -i env PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py \
    --port /dev/cu.<name>            # add --gps if it was set up
```

- Start it parked, engine running. It needs no input; a status line prints every 5 s.
- A passenger watches the status line, or nobody does. Never the driver.
- Drive a mix: a cold start if possible, idle, town, a highway stretch, a stop.
- Ctrl-C ends the session cleanly. A crash loses at most a second; a closed lid stops
  logging until it is opened again.
- A Bluetooth drop shows as `link_lost` and the logger reconnects by itself.

## Afterward

1. Check the capture (rates, gaps and events per PID):

   ```sh
   PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdsum.py data/drive-*.jsonl
   ```

   A `multi_ecu` event means more than one controller answered that PID; its samples
   keep every line in `raw_all` (D-044). Note which PIDs it names: that list decides how
   the analysis picks one controller's reading.

2. Look at it: `tools/obdplot.py` (PNG figures in `data/plots/`), `tools/obdview.py`
   (an offline HTML page per drive) and `tools/obdbins.py` (how well each rpm and load
   cell is filled), each run the same way as `obdsum.py`.
3. Paste the survey's markdown block, from `data/pidscan-*-live.md`, into
   `docs/hardware/pid-survey.md` under the Forester column.
4. Keep the full logs out of git (`data/` is ignored). Commit a short excerpt as
   evidence in its own commit, with the `obdsum` output. If the drive used `--gps`, leave
   the `gps` lines out of the excerpt: they show where the car is parked at home.
5. Tick `pidforester`, `firstcap` and `baseline` yourself when they are true, then run
   `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.

## If the Mac cannot see the adapter: use the Pi

On the Pi, with the car running and the LX in the port:

```sh
bluetoothctl            # then: power on, scan on, pair <MAC>, trust <MAC>, quit
sudo rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1
ls -l /dev/rfcomm0
```

Then run the same two commands with `--port /dev/rfcomm0`, without `caffeinate`, which is
macOS only. If opening the port is refused, add the user to the `dialout` group (`sudo
usermod -aG dialout $USER`, then log in again). Record the MAC address in
`docs/hardware/wiring.md`.

## Results

| Date | Port name | Survey file | Drive file | Samples/s | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| | | | | | |

content.text:
I measured `DESIGN.md` and checked the drive run book, the transcript copy-out steps and the submission rules. Below are both reports: first everything needed to submit by 8 pm, then what to tell Lance.

# Report 1: everything needed to submit TP-D2 by 8 pm

**What the zip is graded on:**

| Points | Criterion | Graded from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | **M2:** design document, both sensors electrically alive, transcripts copied out | the design doc PDF, the sensor evidence, the transcripts |
| 10 | **M3:** both sensors through the real pipeline into real storage, one mechanism working, transcripts | the short video, since there's no live demo for this submission |

### 0. Confirm first (5 min)

- [ ] **Exact deadline and where it goes:** 8 pm today, on Canvas, as one zip. The handout only gives a format for M5 (a tar file), so if the M2 announcement doesn't name the zip's contents, ask the TA. That's board item #161.

### 1. Sensor evidence: the Forester drive (about 1.5 h, and it is also the video shoot)

**At the desk (10 min):**
- [ ] Run `make toolcheck`. It builds the Python environment the tools need.
- [ ] Rehearse once against the simulator: `PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py --sim --max-seconds 20`. You should see about 20 samples a second.
- [ ] Charge the laptop and open QuickTime so screen recording is ready.

**In the car, parked, engine running (10 min):**
- [ ] Plug in the LX, pair it in Bluetooth settings, then run `ls /dev/cu.*` and note the port name.
- [ ] Run `PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/pidscan.py --port /dev/cu.<name>`. **Record the screen.**
- [ ] Start `caffeinate -i env PYTHONPATH=tools .venv/bin/python tools/obdlog.py --port /dev/cu.<name>`. **Record a minute while parked**, revving the engine so rpm visibly moves.

**Drive (20–30 min):**
- [ ] Drive a mix of idle, town, highway and a stop. **The driver never touches the laptop.** A passenger films or nobody does.

**Afterward (20 min):**
- [ ] Run `tools/obdsum.py data/drive-*.jsonl` and `tools/obdplot.py` on the log. **Record both.**
- [ ] Paste the survey block from `data/pidscan-*-live.md` into [pid-survey.md](docs/hardware/pid-survey.md) under the Forester column.
- [ ] Fill in the Results row in [first-drive.md](docs/hardware/first-drive.md).
- [ ] Commit a short excerpt of the log plus the `obdsum` output as evidence, on its own branch, with a draft PR. Leave out any GPS lines.

**If the adapter fails:** use the Pi fallback in `first-drive.md`. If that fails too, film `obdsim` (labeled `synth`) and say so plainly. Don't let it eat the evening.

**The DS18B20 can't be "alive" today, because it hasn't been ordered.** Say so in the design doc (§7) and in the video. Expect to lose part of the "both sensors" points. That's better than any workaround that looks like evidence it isn't.

### 2. The video (about 30 min to cut, 3–5 minutes long)

| # | Shot | About | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | What carwatch is, one sentence over the box or dongle | 20 s | context |
| 2 | Dongle in the port, pairing, `pidscan` output | 30 s | real car, real Mode 01 |
| 3 | `obdlog` streaming while you rev; zoom in on `src=live` | 45 s | live capture, labeled |
| 4 | `obdsum` table and one `obdplot` figure | 30 s | data on disk, rates |
| 5 | `make test`, narrating `test_wal` (cuts the log at every byte; recovery keeps exactly the committed batches) and `test_storaged` (`kill -9` mid-stream; every record lands exactly once) | 60 s | **mechanism D working** |
| 6 | Honest status: the C reader isn't connected to `storaged` yet, the probe isn't ordered, and what the M3 live demo will show | 20 s | integrity |

- [ ] Export as MP4 and check the file size against Canvas's limit. Compress with QuickTime's 1080p or 720p export if needed.

### 3. The design doc (about 1.5 h, ideally with Lance)

**Page budget:** I rendered [DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md) with every 🟨/📏 note and the review box removed (11 pt, letter, 0.75 in margins). It comes to **exactly 5 pages**. Anything you add has to be offset by a cut.

- [ ] **§1 and §5 📏:** replace the estimates with the drive's numbers: requests per second, reply time p50 and p99, and PID count, all from `obdsum`.
- [ ] **§3 🟨:** confirm or replace each fault-area row. Strike any sensor the Forester survey shows it doesn't publish.
- [ ] **§6 🟨:** for each power figure, either give a number or mark it "estimate." Decide the charger-live, engine-silent policy, or name it as open.
- [ ] **§7:** add a row saying the DS18B20 isn't in hand at M2, and what that costs.
- [ ] **§8 🟨:** agree the target numbers (D-036) or change them. M5 is judged against these.
- [ ] **§9 🟨:** fill the ownership map: who takes `obd`, `ambient`, `analysis`, `supervisor`, `interface`, `train` and `electricalDrawing`.
- [ ] **Decisions:** every decision the doc cites is still unsigned. Each of you signs the ones you agree with **in your own commit**. At minimum, sign the ones the doc rests on: D-017, D-021, D-022, D-024, D-025, D-031, D-034, D-035, D-036 and D-037.
- [ ] Delete the review box and every 🟨/📏 note.
- [ ] Run the three-isolated-workers check (design-only reader, BOM-only buyer, wiring-only builder). I can run it as three fresh-context agents.
- [ ] Lint, open a PR, have a human merge it, then render the PDF from the merged version. Chrome's Print → Save as PDF on GitHub's rendered page works, and so does my headless render.

### 4. Transcripts (10 min each)

- [ ] **Camden:** after this session, run `/exit` and then the one-liner in [transcripts/README.md](partners/camden/transcripts/README.md). Commit it on a branch, not `main`.
- [ ] **Lance:** copy out everything since Sep 23 from his own machine, in his own clone, and commit it himself.
- [ ] Board item #35 (`tx2`) gets ticked once both are in.

### 5. Board hygiene (5 min, not graded directly)

- [ ] Tick the work the merged PRs already finished: #38, #39, #40 and #170 to #173.
- [ ] Tick `firstcap`, `pidforester` and `baseline` once they're true after the drive.
- [ ] Run `python3 tools/board_sync.py`.

### 6. Assemble the zip (15 min; aim to upload by 7:45)

```text
carwatch-TPD2-Thomas-Baron.zip
├── DESIGN.pdf
├── carwatch-M3-preview.mp4
├── evidence/   pidscan-*-live.md, obdsum output, drive excerpt, make + make test output
├── transcripts/camden/*.jsonl   transcripts/lance/*.jsonl
└── README.txt  repo URL + commit hash, what each file is, the honest gaps
```

**Don't make a "submission" commit pair.** The handout gives both partners a process grade of zero for that. Everything goes in as normal, purposeful commits.

### If time runs short, in priority order

1. Both partners' transcripts.
2. The design doc PDF with the notes removed. Estimates are fine if they're labeled "estimate."
3. The video. Even `obdsim` plus `make test` is worth something.
4. The real drive data.

# Report 2: what to tell Lance

**1. Where the project is (2 min).** carwatch is a Pi box that reads the car's engine sensors over the Bluetooth OBD2 dongle. It learns this car's normal for each operating point and names the fault area: cooling, air/fuel, or sensor/electrical. There's no cloud. We're graded on mechanisms D and E.

**2. What you've built since he last checked in (2 min):**

The part, its backup cell or capacitor, and that backup's temperature rating are chosen in
`rtcspec`.

## DS18B20 probe → Pi (D-037)

| Probe wire | Pi pin | Pi signal | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DQ (data) | 7 | GPIO4 | The default pin of the kernel's `w1-gpio` overlay. A 4.7 kΩ pull-up from DQ to 3.3 V. |
| VDD | 1 or 17 | 3.3 V | Powered, not parasite mode. Never 5 V: the data line would pull the GPIO above 3.3 V. |
| GND | 9 | GND | |

Pins and the resistor are the 1-Wire defaults, to be checked against the probe's datasheet
and drawn in the Pi interface block (`schpi`) before wiring. Probe wire colors vary by
seller; identify them from the seller's sheet, not by color. The probe sits outside the
shell, in cabin air, away from the Pi's heat.

## Bring-up order

1. Pi on the bench, dongle powered, no car: `bluetoothctl` pairs and trusts it, then
   `rfcomm bind 0 <MAC> 1`, `ls -l /dev/obd`, and `ATZ` answers with the dongle's
   version string. Reboot once and confirm `/dev/obd` comes back without a hand.
2. Car, key to run, engine off: `0100` returns the supported-PID bitmap.
3. Car, engine running: `010C` (RPM) changes when you touch the throttle.
4. Probe, Pi on the bench: `dtoverlay=w1-gpio` in `/boot/firmware/config.txt`, reboot,
   then `cat /sys/bus/w1/devices/28-*/w1_slave` shows `YES` on the first line and a
   `t=` value near room temperature on the second. Paste it here, dated (`probebench`).
5. The power measurements above: the free ones first (the owner's charger with a meter,
   key off and at crank), the bank only after the power design is signed.

Measured results go in this file, dated. A step without a recorded result has not been
done (CLAUDE.md §8.4).

    out = {}
    for key, p in sorted(pids.items()):
        times, vals = p["times"], p["vals"]
        gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:])]
        out[key] = {
            "name": obdlib.pid_name(int(key, 16)), "unit": p["unit"], "n": len(times),
            "hz": len(times) / seconds if seconds else 0.0,
            "min": min(vals) if vals else None, "max": max(vals) if vals else None,
            "mean": statistics.fmean(vals) if vals else None,
            "max_gap": max(gaps) if gaps else 0.0,
            "no_data": p["no_data"], "errors": p["errors"],
        }
    return {
        "src": src, "adapter": header.get("adapter"),
        "protocol": header.get("protocol"), "vin_hash": header.get("vin_hash"),
        "seconds": seconds, "samples": len(samples),
        "rate": len(samples) / seconds if seconds else 0.0,
        "gps": sum(1 for r in records if r["type"] == "gps"),
        "ended": footer["reason"] if footer else "no footer (session did not end cleanly)",
        "events": events, "pids": out,
    }


def _f(v, width=8):
    return f"{v:{width}.2f}" if v is not None else " " * (width - 1) + "-"


def render(s, path, torn=False):
    lines = [f"== {path}"]
    if s["src"] != "live":
        lines.append(f"!! {s['src'].upper()} DATA: not from a real car")
    lines += [
        f"src={s['src']}  adapter={s['adapter']}  protocol={s['protocol']}  "
        f"vin_hash={s['vin_hash']}",
        f"{s['seconds']:.1f} s, {s['samples']} samples, {s['rate']:.1f} samples/s, "
        f"{s['gps']} gps fixes, ended: {s['ended']}" + (", torn last line" if torn else ""),
        "",
        f"{'PID':4} {'signal':32} {'n':>6} {'Hz':>6} {'min':>8} {'mean':>8} {'max':>8} "
        f"{'unit':6} {'gap s':>6} {'nodata':>6} {'errors':>6}",
    ]
    for key, p in s["pids"].items():
        lines.append(f"{key:4} {p['name'][:32]:32} {p['n']:6d} {p['hz']:6.2f} "
                     f"{_f(p['min'])} {_f(p['mean'])} {_f(p['max'])} {p['unit']:6} "
                     f"{p['max_gap']:6.2f} {p['no_data']:6d} {p['errors']:6d}")
    lines.append("")
    lines.append("events: " + (", ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(s["events"].items()))
                               or "none"))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("logs", nargs="+")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    for path in args.logs:
        records, torn = obdlog.read_log(path)
        print(render(summarize(records), path, torn))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

            out.write("sample", pid=key, raw=raws[0], val=value, unit=unit,
                      n_ecu=len(raws), **extra)
            counts["samples"] += 1

            poll_gps()
            status()
    except BaseException as e:
        failure = f"error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
